deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up the complex logarithm as an integral and derives its addition law.

(1) Polar form of dz/z. Write z = r e^{iφ}. Then dz = e^{iφ} dr + i r e^{iφ} dφ, so dz/z = dr/r + i dφ. Integrating gives ∫ dz/z = ∫ (dr/r + i dφ) = log r + φ i. In other words the integral is log|z| + i·arg z, the complex logarithm. Its imaginary part depends on how much angle the path sweeps around 0.

(2) The sketch. It shows two perpendicular axes (the complex plane) and a horizontal segment with a slanted segment rising from it. This is most plausibly an integration path: from 1 along the real axis, then off it toward s. That fits the decomposition into a radial part (dr/r) and an angular part (i dφ).

(3) Definition. ψ(s) := ∫_1^s dz/z, so ψ is the logarithm, normalised by ψ(1) = 0.

(4) Additivity of the path integral. ψ(ss') = ∫_1^{ss'} dz/z = ∫_1^s dz/z + ∫_s^{ss'} dz/z. The integrand is written dz/dz on the page; this is a slip for dz/z.

(5) Implicit next step (mine, certain in intent). Substitute z = s w in the second integral. Then dz/z = dw/w, and the limits s → ss' become 1 → s'. So ∫_s^{ss'} dz/z = ψ(s'), giving ψ(ss') = ψ(s) + ψ(s').

Purpose: to derive the functional equation of the logarithm from its integral definition in the complex domain. That equation holds only modulo 2πi, depending on the paths chosen. This is elementary groundwork for the theory of complex functions and multivalued integrals.
errors: Slip of the pen: the left integrand in the last line is written dz/dz instead of dz/z.

The equality ψ(ss') = ψ(s) + ψ(s') (implied, not written) holds only modulo 2πi unless paths are fixed consistently. The page does not address the path dependence of the φ term, though the polar decomposition makes it visible.
The last line shows only the splitting of the path; the substitution z = s w that finishes the argument is not written.

results.what: dz/z = dr/r + i dφ for z = r e^{iφ}, so ∫dz/z = log r + iφ (complex logarithm as an integral)
results.modern_name: Complex logarithm Log z = ln|z| + i arg z defined by ∫_1^z dt/t
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (complex logarithm, 1740s); integral and path view from Cauchy (1820s)

results.what: ψ(s) = ∫_1^s dz/z satisfies ψ(ss') = ψ(s) + ψ(s') via path additivity and the substitution z = s w
results.modern_name: Functional equation of the logarithm derived from its integral definition

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary, standard facts about the complex logarithm. Riemann's 1851 dissertation already treats logarithms and multivalued integrals in the complex plane, so nothing here is new or unexpected.
